coverage: Whole-group totals · one reported business segment (steel)
definition: Profit for the year after all expenses, exceptional items and tax, including a large one-time gain. It includes profit that belongs to minority owners of subsidiaries and is not operating profit or cash flow.
location: Integrated Annual Report 2025–26, consolidated statement of profit and loss: PDF page 287 (page header 570/571); note 48 exceptional items: PDF pages 339–340; note 42 segment reporting: PDF page 325
notes: Revenue is revenue from operations and excludes other income of ₹1,248 crore. Profit for the year is ₹25,508 crore, of which ₹22,316 crore belongs to owners of JSW Steel and ₹3,192 crore to non-controlling interests. Exceptional items were a net gain of ₹17,359 crore: a gain of ₹18,051 crore recorded on 27 March 2026 when JSW Steel lost control of the Bhushan Power and Steel business by putting it into a 50:50 joint venture with JFE Steel of Japan, less ₹692 crore for the new Labour Codes (higher employee-benefit obligations). A further ₹2,301 crore of that gain is deferred and will be recognised later. Profit before exceptional items and tax was ₹11,891 crore; tax was ₹3,742 crore. The group reports steel manufacturing as a single reportable segment, so no profit by product is shown. Revenue by customer location: ₹158,569 crore within India and ₹26,901 crore outside India.
insight: Most of JSW Steel’s reported profit this year comes from a one-time accounting gain on the Bhushan Power and Steel joint venture rather than from selling steel. Profit before that gain and tax was ₹11,891 crore, which is a fairer guide to the underlying business.
